3: Customers want different things, and rivals react. Good service is harder to copy than a low price.
4: Profit isn't cash. Stock, unpaid invoices and loans move cash without changing profit.
5: Growth costs money first. Loans must be repaid; investors take a share instead.
6: Know your break-even, protect your cash, listen to customers, grow at your cash's pace.
cafe-1: Price sets how many buy, and making too much or too little both cost money.
cafe-2: Fixed costs come first. Break-even says how many customers you need; runway says how long you can wait.
saas-1: Subscriptions stack up month after month. The best price balances sign-ups and revenue each.
saas-2: Growing software loses money at first. It works when customers are worth well over their cost to win.
shop-1: Stock turns cash into goods. Profit counts bags sold; your bank pays for every bag bought.
shop-2: Every order has hidden costs. Ads pay only when their profit beats their cost.
agency-1: You sell your time. The right rate fills your hours without leaving money on the table.
agency-2: Salaries are paid either way. Keeping people busy covers your fixed costs.
idea: Your numbers decide if the idea works. Check break-even and runway first.
